findings.title: Preview planning spawns into the actual graph (P1, defect)
Patch records the transaction after changing the pin (P1, defect)
Patch silently drops requested links in mixed updates (P1, defect)
Replace is two committed edits, not one atomic replacement (P1, defect)
Rollback claims do not depend on rollback success (P1, defect; nested-transaction risk)
Safe call swap resets unlinked arguments (P1, defect in dirty implementation)
Write-readiness is advisory, not an enforced graph guard (P1, defect in advertised guard coverage)
Repoint refuses normal occupied data-input migration (P2 defect; engine response requires live confirmation)
Source deletion is wider than the repointed output (P1 risk/defect in dirty implementation)
Node identity is inconsistent and unstable across collision-width changes (P2)
Compile/readback success is much narrower than validity (P1 safety gap)
Batch rollback wording and plan staleness (P2, untracked implementation)
Shared pure-node definitions are never emitted (P2, definite reader omission)
Quoting is not a reversible grammar (P2, defect)
Read output is not a complete graph serialization (unsupported, with destructive-use risk)
Node creation/type identity and wildcards need additional safety proof (P2 risks)
Dirty-state observation is not independent proof of a durable package write (P2 risk)
Release gate can report success without successful acceptance
Client retries mutations after ambiguous failures
Unfinished batch edit is publicly reflected
Test gates are heuristic, not semantic coverage
Four toolset classes do not enforce read-only behavior
Tool failures can be MCP successes
String-only inputs and incomplete help increase agent mistakes
Packaging dependencies remain incomplete
Setup is not a reproducible release install
Lifecycle scripts can stop unrelated editors
Build success can still mean no plugin artifact
Logging is useful, but not a reliable mutation ledger
Security boundary must be local and explicit
Documentation and board state are not release evidence
Material tidy Preview recompiles and dirties the material.
Widget Look preview runs unrestricted zero-parameter functions and widget construction logic without isolation; transient allocation does not guarantee read-only behavior.
Trace attribution uses bytecode offset zero, not the executing instruction. Zero-hit conclusions are unsound.
Play-check can report a completed play window even when the start witness never fired.
Explicit reference direction `both` skips both queries and reports zero/zero.
Data-table set-then-remove batches recreate the row and can report success.
Blueprint `private` variables use EditConst instead of the engine's private metadata; external Blueprint access is not restricted as requested.
Struct default setters can refuse values, but return values are discarded and success output does not verify defaults.
Material tidy ignores rollback failure and does not snapshot the material collection before adding comments.
